caveats: **macOS product-name/version reads never shell out today.** Wave 3/PR31 (2026-08-19) moved `os_name`/`os_version`/`os_build` off `sw_vers` onto `SystemVersion.plist` + `sysctlbyname`, reaching ADR-3002 rung 1 with zero spawned processes (`changelog.d/20260819-wave3-pr31-syscall-promotion.changed.md`); the definition YAML's prose describing `sw_vers` for these three fields was stale and is fixed as part of this documentation pass.

**`uptime_seconds` can emit a non-numeric string despite its declared `int64` type.** When the platform read fails (`/proc/uptime` unreadable on Linux, the `KERN_BOOTTIME` sysctl failing on macOS), the leg writes the literal `unknown` instead of an integer (`os_info_plugin.cpp:371-377`); no sample in this capture set hit that path.

**`os_product_version` is macOS-only and conditionally emitted.** It rides a second `write_output` call inside `#ifdef __APPLE__` on the `os_version` action (`os_info_plugin.cpp:251-256`); Windows and Linux responses for `os_version` carry only one row.

**`os_arch` is not normalized on Linux/macOS.** Those legs return the raw `uname().machine` string verbatim (e.g. `aarch64` vs `arm64` — not the same token); only the Windows leg maps to a fixed `x86_64`/`aarch64`/`x86`/`arm`/`unknown` set (`os_info_plugin.cpp:311-343`).

**The plist parser is deliberately not a general XML parser.** `os_info_macos.hpp` scans for a flat `<dict>` of sibling `<key>/<string>` pairs only, because `SystemVersion.plist` is Apple-authored and not adversarial input; it returns `nullopt` on any nesting or a nearer sibling tag rather than guessing (`os_info_macos.hpp:14-19,48-55`).

definitions.description: Returns the CPU architecture of the endpoint (e.g. "x86_64", "aarch64", "arm"). On Windows, uses GetNativeSystemInfo. On Linux and macOS, uses uname().machine.

Returns the OS build identifier. On Windows, reports CurrentBuildNumber.UBR from the registry (e.g. "22631.4890"). On Linux, extracts the kernel build version from /proc/version. On macOS, reads ProductBuildVersion from SystemVersion.plist, falling back to the kern.osversion sysctl -- no subprocess is spawned.

Returns the full OS product name (e.g. "Windows 11 Pro", "Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS", "macOS 26.6.2"). On Windows, reads the registry ProductName and corrects the Windows 10/11 naming for builds >= 22000. On Linux, reads PRETTY_NAME from /etc/os-release. On macOS, reads ProductName and ProductVersion from SystemVersion.plist, falling back to the kern.osproductversion sysctl and then a literal if the plist is unreadable -- no subprocess is spawned.

Returns the OS version string. On Windows, reports Major.Minor.Build from RtlGetVersion (avoids manifest-dependent version lies). On Linux and macOS, reports the kernel release from uname. On macOS, also returns the user-facing product version (os_product_version) read from SystemVersion.plist's ProductVersion key, falling back to the kern.osproductversion sysctl -- no subprocess is spawned.
Returns the system uptime in seconds and a human-readable display string (e.g. "12d 5h 23m"). Uses /proc/uptime on Linux, kern.boottime sysctl on macOS, GetTickCount64 on Windows.

description: Reports OS name, version, build, architecture, and system uptime
how_it_works:
All five actions are single reads, no parameters. `os_name` builds the human-facing product name: Linux reads `PRETTY_NAME` from `/etc/os-release`; macOS reads `ProductName`/`ProductVersion` from `SystemVersion.plist` (sysctl and literal fallbacks); Windows reads the registry `ProductName` and corrects the Windows 10→11 naming lie for builds ≥ 22000. `os_version` reports the kernel/OS version — `uname(2)` release on Linux/macOS, `RtlGetVersion` on Windows (avoids `GetVersionEx`'s manifest-dependent lies) — and on macOS additionally emits a second row, the user-facing `os_product_version`. `os_build` reads `/proc/version` (Linux), `SystemVersion.plist`'s `ProductBuildVersion` (macOS), or `CurrentBuildNumber`+`UBR` from the registry (Windows). `os_arch` reads `uname(2).machine` on Linux/macOS (raw, unnormalized) or maps `GetNativeSystemInfo` to a fixed token set on Windows. `uptime` reads `/proc/uptime`, the `KERN_BOOTTIME` sysctl, or `GetTickCount64`, and always emits both a raw second count and a formatted display string.

Every leg is native in-process (ADR-3002 rung 1, zero subprocesses) — including macOS, which read `sw_vers` output until the Wave 3/PR31 syscall promotion moved it onto `SystemVersion.plist` + `sysctlbyname`. The plugin deliberately does not persist OS identity as a typed daily-sync inventory record; it is a live/on-demand read surface only, and it never sets a typed result status.
name: os_info

columns.description: CPU architecture. Linux and macOS report the raw uname(2) machine string unnormalized (e.g. "aarch64", "arm64" -- not the same token); Windows maps GetNativeSystemInfo to a fixed set: x86_64, aarch64, x86, arm, or unknown. Values: free text (Linux/macOS); "x86_64", "aarch64", "x86", "arm", "unknown" (Windows).
columns.name: os_arch

columns.description: The OS build identifier: registry CurrentBuildNumber.UBR on Windows; the third whitespace field of /proc/version on Linux; SystemVersion.plist's ProductBuildVersion (sysctl kern.osversion fallback) on macOS. Values: free text.
columns.name: os_build

columns.description: The OS product name as read by the platform-specific leg (registry ProductName on Windows, corrected for the Windows 11 naming quirk; PRETTY_NAME from /etc/os-release on Linux; ProductName + ProductVersion from SystemVersion.plist on macOS). Values: free text.
columns.name: os_name

columns.description: The kernel/version string: Major.Minor.Build from RtlGetVersion on Windows; the uname(2) kernel release on Linux and macOS. Values: free text.
columns.name: os_version

columns.description: macOS-only: the user-facing product version read from SystemVersion.plist's ProductVersion key (sysctl kern.osproductversion fallback); not emitted on Windows or Linux. Values: free text.
columns.name: os_product_version

columns.description: Seconds since boot. Emitted as the literal string "unknown" instead of an integer if the platform read fails (/proc/uptime unreadable on Linux, the KERN_BOOTTIME sysctl failing on macOS) -- never observed in this capture set. Values: integer, or the literal "unknown".
columns.name: uptime_seconds

columns.description: Human-readable uptime formatted "<days>d <hours>h <minutes>m"; "unknown" if the platform read failed. Values: free text ("<n>d <n>h <n>m"), or the literal "unknown".
columns.name: uptime_display

outputs_note: Pipe-delimited `key|value` lines via `write_output()` — no row discriminator (unlike a multi-row action, each call emits one fixed set of known keys). A key is always present; when the underlying read fails the value is the literal `unknown` rather than the key being omitted.

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows land in the ResponseStore over the agent's command-response channel; `os_info` is in the `kKeyValuePlugins` set (`server/core/src/result_parsing.hpp:63`), so SSE row rendering, ResponseStore facet extraction, and DashboardRoutes fragment rendering all render it as an `Agent · Key · Value` table.

**Live snapshot / device dashboard.** `uptime` is one of two allow-listed "Get live info" kinds (`server/core/src/live_kinds.hpp:43`, `resolve_kind("uptime") → LiveKind{"os_info","uptime",...}`), dispatched as a real, deliberately **untracked** instruction (no `ExecutionTracker` row — `server/core/src/server.cpp:19704`) and rendered as a KPI tile (`server/core/src/device_routes.hpp:130`). Reachable via `POST /api/v1/dex/devices/{id}/live?kind=uptime` (`server/core/src/rest_api_v1.cpp:10424-10437`).

**Pre-flight (`/auto`) gate.** `os_version` and `os_arch` are two of the five blocking Slice-1 checks, parsed by raw pipe-field index — bypassing `result.columns` entirely (`server/core/src/preflight_parse.hpp:13-15,51-52`).

**Not consumed by** daily-sync, the TAR warehouse, or typed inventory: `is_typed_inventory_source` (`server/core/src/typed_inventory_sources.hpp:22-26`) lists only `installed_software`, `app_perf`, `device_ci`, `software_licensing` — `os_info` is absent, so its result never lands in a typed daily-sync store.
**Sensitivity.** Rows carry only OS name/version/build/architecture and uptime — no device id, MAC, hostname, username, or installed-software identifier appears in any field.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("device.os_info.uptime")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}` for an instruction dispatch; `/api/v1/dex/devices/{id}/live?kind=uptime` for the live KPI path.
